To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of a backtracked RNA-dependent RNA polymerization intermediate of norovirus polymerases has been determined, which reveals conformational states of the polymerase similar to those following nucleotide incorporation and provides insight into the mechanism for RNA translocation following the nucleotidyl-transfer reaction.

the structure of a backtracked complex of NV RdRP reveals conformational similarities with the pre-incorporation state of the enzyme and suggests that a conformational change of the thumb domain may be involved in RNA translocation following incorporation.
the structure of the human norovirus RNA polymerase reveals a conformational state that resembles the post-incorporation state in which RNA translocation occurs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, evolution, and antiviral drug design of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRPs) from positive-strand RNA viruses.
the structural biology of human norovirus (hNoV) and its polymerase.
the structure and function of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRPs) and their roles in RNA virus replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BACK1 structure is a snapshot of a post-nucleotide-incorporation complex, which is a step in the enzymatic cycle of the NV RdRP.
the BACK1 structure represents an intermediate state in the enzymatic cycle of NV polymerase between the PRE1 and POST1 states.
the BACK1 structure is a hybrid of the closed PRE1 and open APO1 states, and thus reveals a complex pathway of con-formational changes that may be unique to NV RdRP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BACK1 structure provides insight into the conformational changes in the polymerase during the RNA translocation step, and the comparison of BACK1 with the APO1 and PRE1 structures suggests that the polymerase may be in a state similar to a transition state between the open and closed states.
we solved the structure of a novel backtracked state for the NV polymerase, which is the first time that such a structure has been reported for any RNA virus RdRP.
the BACK1 complex reveals an open-to-closed transition of the thumb domain that is distinct from the closed-to-open transition seen in the APO1 to PRE1 transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single RdRP polymerase can adopt multiple conformations and that each conformational state can be stabilized by different crystal contacts.
the thumb domain of RdRp can be open while the polymerase is active, and the thumb domain can be open even when the polymerase is in a backtracked or post-incorporation state.
a backtracked state of the polymerase can be trapped in a crystal and that the backtracked state has a structure that is very similar to the post-incorporation state.
